chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Al-Maghrib during the journey is up to a third of the night, and it is also reported as up to half the night.'
ai.seo_question: What is the extended time for Maghrib prayer during travel according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the extended window for Maghrib prayer during travel, citing Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) as the source. The variance between a third and half of the night reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *tawassul* (expansion of time) for travelers, allowing flexibility based on ease and necessity. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing the travel-specific legal status (*hukm al-musafir*) from that of the resident (*muqim*).
